title: Peer-Reviewed Machine-Learning Study Strengthens the VASCO Research Debate
author: Stephen Bruehl, Brian Doherty, Alina Streblyanska and Beatriz Villarroel
summary: A peer-reviewed study trained a machine-learning classifier to distinguish likely astronomical transients from plate defects and reports that debated nuclear-window and Earth-shadow patterns persist after probability-based artifact control. The study does not determine the candidates’ physical origin.

image.alt: Scientific editorial illustration of paired historical astronomical plates being analyzed by a machine-learning system to distinguish transient point sources from scratches and plate defects.
